text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture, as leaders Liverpool go to the Gtech Community Stadium to face Brentford!

For the first time in many years, it looks like we have a real three-horse title race on our hands in the Premier League, and this weekend, Liverpool get the chance to pull five points clear at the summit as they play before Manchester City and Arsenal.

Jurgen Klopp's side bounced back from their 3-1 defeat at the Emirates Stadium by beating Burnley by the same scoreline last week, but they come into this game with a few selection issues, with the likes of Alisson, Trent Alexander-Arnold and Dominik Szoboszlai out.
They do, however, have Mohamed Salah available, six weeks on from his last club appearance.
The leaders will face a tough test in west London, though, on a ground where they were beaten 3-1 last season.

Brentford looked to be in danger of slipping into the thick of the relegation battle, but Ivan Toney's return from an eight-month ban has provoked an upturn in their fortunes, and he was on the scoresheet as the Bees recorded an impressive 2-0 win at Wolves last week.
Thomas Frank's men enter Matchday 25 with a six-point buffer to the bottom three, and they will be desperate to put more ground between themselves and their rivals here.
Frank makes just one change to the Brentford team that won at Molineux last week.
That switch comes in the heart of defence as Ajer replaces the injured Ethan Pinnock, but the Bees have received a double boost elsewhere.
Wissa and Onyeka are both named among the substitutes after returning from the Africa Cup of Nations, with Maupay holding off a challenge from the former to keep his place alongside Toney.
Klopp, meanwhile, makes two changes to the Liverpool XI which started last week's win over Burnley.
Alexander-Arnold is out with a knee injury which will also sideline him for next week's EFL Cup final, meaning Bradley returns at right-back.
Konate returns from suspension to replace Quansah at centre-back, but Kelleher continues in goal after Alisson reportedly suffered a hamstring injury in training on Friday.
There are plenty of big names on the Reds' bench, not least the returning Salah, who has recovered from the hamstring issue which ended his Africa Cup of Nations campaign.
The players are out at the Gtech Community Stadium! Kick-off is just moments away!
We're under way in west London as Liverpool – donning their all purple change kit – get the ball rolling through Nunez!

Klopp famously isn't keen on these early Saturday kick-offs, but Liverpool are unbeaten in their four Premier League games taking place at 12:30pm on a Saturday this season (three wins, one draw), having failed to win any of their six such matches last term (three draws, three losses).
A poor pass from Jota stops a Liverpool break in its tracks, and Brentford come forward through Jensen.
He crosses low from the right and Van Dijk is forced to make the block, then Diaz gets back to recover possession.
WIDE! The first chance goes Brentford's way! The home fans aren't happy as Konate is all over Maupay, but the Frenchman does well to hold the ball up and work it infield to Norgaard.
He finds Janelt in space, and the midfielder drags a poor left-footed effort well wide – he should have done better!
Brentford have made a very positive start here! Reguilon almost bursts onto a reverse pass into the box from Maupay, and Van Dijk is forced to put his foot through the ball.
Liverpool are being penned back early on.
Action at both ends! Janelt looks to break in behind with Liverpool caught upfield, and Van Dijk is forced into another booming clearance.
Liverpool then attack down their right through Nunez, but there's nobody there to tap his low cross home – it only needed a touch!
Jota – the Premier League's Player of the Month for January – carries the ball through the centre of the field and looks to release Nunez, but Mee closes him down and blocks the pass.
We've had a high-octane start to this one!
DOUBLE SAVE! Bradley almost gets his second Premier League goal, drifting infield before prodding an audacious attempt towards the bottom-right corner, using the outside of his boot.
Flekken does brilliantly to push it away, then he gets up to make himself big and smother Jota's follow-up!
Liverpool have both scored and conceded in all seven of their away league games against Brentford.
They lost 3-1 here last season but have never lost successive away matches against the Bees before.
Should we expect plenty of goalmouth action?
Liverpool are starting to enjoy more possession now.
Robertson looks to hang a cross up with Mac Allister hitting the area, but it drifts all the way through to Flekken.
Nunez tries to trick his way down the left wing and wins a corner for Liverpool.
Robertson's kick is headed clear inside a crowded six-yard box, then Jota is just unable to reach the second delivery into the box.
There's a brief VAR check on a possible penalty for Liverpool, as Janelt seemed to have a hold of Jota, wrestling the Portugal international to the ground in advance of the corner being delivered.
The check is quickly cleared, and Brentford might have gotten away with one there...

WIDE! Maupay and Toney are causing Liverpool problems here! The former drops deep before rolling a clever pass into the path of Toney, who sends his left-footed finish across goal and narrowly wide of the bottom-right corner.
Unlucky!
It's another positive moment for Brentford as Toney tries to break into the area, being caught by Mac Allister right on the line.
Michael Oliver points for a free-kick, rather than a penalty, and the VAR agrees with that call.
It's still a promising position for Toney, though...
Straight at the goalkeeper! Toney's effort is a poor one and Kelleher is totally untroubled in the centre of his goal.
Since Toney's first Premier League appearance of the season on January 20, only three players have more goals in the division than he does (three in four games).
Liverpool are, however, one of four teams he has faced without ever scoring in the competition (three games, seven shots, one shot on target).
Robertson surges down the left before firing off a cross, but it's overhit and Bradley has to work to keep it alive on the far side.
He works it infield to Diaz, who in turn sends it back to the left, and another Robertson delivery is headed out by Mee.
Brentford are defending very well here.
SAVE! Brentford continue to threaten on the break.
Toney is sent racing into the right-hand channel by Maupay, but Van Dijk sticks with him and his low strike eventually lacks the necessary power to beat Kelleher.
Liverpool are just struggling to get into their rhythm here.
GOOD SAVE! Now it's Liverpool's turn to threaten as Jota brings down a bouncing ball before firing off a shot from the edge of the box, and Flekken springs up to push it over the crossbar.
Corner.
The Brentford fans aren't happy as Endo appears to handle from Robertson's inswinging delivery, but the referee doesn't see it and Liverpool eventually win another corner.
Again, the home defence stands firm, with Ajer stepping in to intercept ahead of Nunez on the edge of the box.
Brentford look to load the area from a deep free-kick, but Mee is just unable to keep it alive at the far post.
Frank will be very happy with how his side have matched Liverpool so far, though, as we pass the 25-minute mark.
What a run from Jota! That's brilliant work from the Portugal forward, whose powerful run takes him past three Brentford challenges, from the halfway line to the edge of the area.
His last touch just runs too long, though, and the home defence can crowd Diaz out as he tries to bring the loose ball in.
Toney takes aim with an audacious attempt from near the right corner of the Liverpool box, but it dribbles well wide of the bottom-left corner.
He was never troubling Kelleher there.
Good move! Maupay has been excellent so far.
A mazy run takes him to the edge of the Liverpool box, where he offloads to Janelt.
His lay-off allows Norgaard to take aim, but his shot dribbles wide of the bottom-left corner.
This is a concern for Liverpool.
Jones lost out in a 50-50 earlier in the move which led to that last Brentford chance, and he has stayed down.
He looks to have gone over on his ankle, and he's still receiving treatment.
Jones is moving very gingerly as he makes his way to the sideline.
It doesn't look like he'll be able to carry on, and Liverpool will soldier on with 10 men until the change can be made.
The pace of the game has just dropped now, after Brentford's fast start and Liverpool's subsequent spell of pressure.
Bradley ups the tempo by racing down the right to cross for Diaz, but a slight touch from a defender takes it away from the Colombian.
Gravenberch enters the action for Liverpool as Jones makes his way around the pitch and towards the tunnel.
With the EFL Cup final on the horizon and Alexander-Arnold and Szoboszlai out, that is a real worry for Klopp.

GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLL! NUNEZ WITH A LOVELY FINISH! What a counterattack from Liverpool! Brentford load the box from a deep free-kick, with Van Dijk hammering a clearance away as the Bees look to make something of a flick-on.
There's just one Brentford defender back as Jota wins a clever header to release Nunez one-on-one, and the Uruguayan nonchalantly scoops the ball over Flekken! 1-0!
What an assist that is from Jota.
The forward is running away from goal in the left-hand channel but still manages to send his header perfectly into the path of Nunez, who does the rest!
Now Diaz looks to break into the box on the right-hand side, but his cutback is smothered by Flekken.
That goal has put a spring in Liverpool's step.
There may be questions asked as to how Brentford left themselves so short-handed at the back from the initial set-piece, though.
After assisting Nunez's opener, Jota has 15 goal involvements across his last 19 away starts in the Premier League for Liverpool (eight goals, seven assists).
Now Jota is down inside the Brentford half, having been come off worse from a collision involving both Norgaard and Mac Allister.
Klopp looks on ruefully, he can't afford any further injuries.
This is a major concern for Liverpool.
Jota attempts to get up before immediately dropping back to the turf, and a stretcher is being brought out.
It looks like Jota was hurt upon landing in that previous challenge, with Norgaard falling on top of him.
Salah is preparing to enter the action – it's not a bad replacement, but this is not the way Liverpool wanted him to make his return.
Jota is carried off on a stretcher as Salah enters the fray.
We will likely have a lengthy amount of first-half stoppage time now.
There's the first booking of the game, and it goes to Reguilon.
The Tottenham loanee dives into a poor challenge on Bradley, catching the youngster on the top of his boot, and deservedly sees yellow.
Almost a brilliant move! Salah's first involvement sees him volley a pass over the top to Nunez, who cushions it back across the box with Diaz lurking.
Fortunately for Brentford, Flekken reaches the pass first.
We are into EIGHT minutes of first-half stoppage time, following those injuries to Jones and Jota.
BIG CHANCE FOR 2-0! Jensen lines up a long throw into the Liverpool box, which causes a scramble before Konate clears.
Diaz has so much space as he drives down the left on the counterattack, before cutting it back for Salah, who just can't sort his feet out as the ball bobbles off his leg and is cleared!
A recurring theme of this game has been Brentford leaving themselves short from their own set-pieces, piling as many players into the box as possible.
They get another dead-ball opportunity out on the left, as Konate pushes Maupay over.
Kelleher makes the catch from the free-kick before looking to set Salah off on the break, but this time, Brentford get men back to recover the long kick out.
Reguilon then gets up the left to cross, and though Toney plucks his overhit delivery out of the air on the far side, he can't stop it drifting behind.
Brentford have managed eight shots to Liverpool's five here, but the Reds are winning the expected goals (xG) battle 1.06-0.32.
The Bees have had plenty of audacious attempts, failing to carve out a clear chance in the last half-hour or so.
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 0-1 LIVERPOOL.
It's half-time at the Gtech Community Stadium, and as things stand, Liverpool are set to move five points clear at the top of the Premier League thanks to Nunez's lovely dinked finish.

The Reds struggled with Brentford's intensity early on but have slowly taken charge of the game, and if not for a couple of good saves from Flekken and a rare miscue from Salah, they might be further ahead.
However, it wasn't all positive for Klopp, as he was forced to use two substitutions to replace the injured Jones and Jota.
With Alisson, Alexander-Arnold and Szoboszlai already out, the Reds' selection issues are piling up.
Frank will be pleased with aspects of Brentford's performance despite the scoreline; Maupay and Toney caused Liverpool problems early on, and the Bees look dangerous from set-pieces.
However, they have also caused their own issues from those same situations, with Liverpool's goal arriving when they left one man back from a deep free-kick, giving Jota and Nunez space on the break.
It was a bit naïve from Frank's usually streetwise side.
Klopp has made a third change at the break, introducing Gakpo for goalscorer Nunez.
Reds fans will be hoping that is not another fitness concern – with two of his three substitution windows used up, it could just be smart management from Klopp.
We're under way for the second half as Brentford get the ball rolling! Is there a way back for the Bees?
There's an injury concern for Brentford now, with Toney down after Bradley's studs appeared to catch him on the back of the calf as the pair contested an aerial duel.
He's still receiving treatment – it looked like a painful one.
Toney will be fine to continue after receiving treatment.
He had to leave the pitch temporarily, but is now allowed back on by referee Oliver.
Only Aston Villa (three) have dropped fewer points from winning positions than Liverpool in the Premier League this season (four).
Brentford, meanwhile, have recovered a middling eight points from losing positions in the Premier League this campaign.
Liverpool should do better! Diaz has space as he advances towards the edge of the box, with Gakpo making a good run off the shoulder of the last defender.
However, Diaz hits his pass with too much power, and Gakpo can't get it out of his feet inside the area.
Over! Now Diaz cuts inside from the left and finds space for a shot, and Flekken looks concerned as it just rises over his crossbar.
Decent effort, but no reward.
HUGE MISS! How is it not 2-0?! Brentford's defensive line is nowhere to be seen again as Salah latches onto a long pass over the top.
He looks destined to double Liverpool's lead as he scampers into the area, but he completely misjudges his finish and dinks it well wide of the near post.
Brentford won't get many more let-offs like that one!
Important defending! For a team known for their solidity, Brentford are giving up so much space on the break.
Liverpool have a three-on-two situation as Salah darts across halfway before electing to go right with his pass to Gakpo.
Gakpo tries to cut it back to Salah, but Janelt gets back in with a vital intervention.
Liverpool have scored more second-half goals than any other side in the Premier League this term (34).
Brentford need to force the issue at some point, but they also need to be wary of their opponents' counterattacking prowess.

GOOOOOOAAAAAAALLL! MAC ALLISTER MAKES IT 2-0! Liverpool have the second goal they have been threatening since the restart! Salah is at the heart of it, taking in Gravenberch's pass before finding Mac Allister's run with a terrific ball into the box.
The Argentine's first touch takes the ball between the legs of Collins, then he slides his finish past the helpless Flekken.
Great goal!
Salah is back with a bang! From an inside-right position, he plays a lovely ball into the D, where Mac Allister breaks onto it, leaves Collins grounded, and prods home!
Almost! Janelt spots Kelleher off his line and goes for goal from inside his own half, and the Liverpool goalkeeper is visibly worried as he darts back.
However, the midfielder's audacious effort drops a couple of yards wide.
Chance, but the flag is up! Brentford fire another deep free-kick towards the danger zone as they seek a response.
Mee wins the first header, then Toney flicks the ball towards goal, but Maupay can only help it onto the roof of the net before seeing the flag raised against him.
Over! The ever-impressive Bradley inverts into a midfield position, taking a touch out of his feet before sending a rasping drive over the crossbar from 25 yards out.
It was only a yard too high.
Brentford have lost four of their last six home Premier League matches, as many as they had in their previous 30 (15 wins, 11 draws, four defeats).
They look destined for another loss here, with Liverpool able to pick their moments to strike on the break at 2-0.
Salah has been directly involved in four goals across his last two Premier League appearances (two goals, two assists), as many as in his previous six games in the competition.
His month-long lay-off doesn't look to have affected him too much.
Liverpool look to be in control now, with the atmosphere falling flat in west London.
Frank is about to respond with two substitutions.
We're going to see the returns of Brentford's two African stars.
Onyeka is on for Norgaard in midfield.
Wissa, meanwhile, is on for Maupay.
He might feel hard done by, having been a menace to Liverpool's defence from the off.
In fact, Frank will make it a triple change, with Lewis-Potter on for Roerslev in a positive switch.
Brentford have done plenty of things well here, but they have certainly caused their own issues.
In the build-up to Liverpool's second goal, a flat kick from Flekken failed to clear the halfway line and was won back by Endo, allowing Liverpool to quickly feed the ball wide to Salah.
Toney gets back in a bid to recover possession for Brentford, but his loose touch only succeeds in teeing Gakpo up for a 20-yard strike.
It's blocked at close quarters, but the ball is soon back with Liverpool.
They're in total control now.
Good move! Gravenberch feeds a pass into Salah inside the Brentford area, and he immediately lays it off to Mac Allister.
Salah wants the ball played back to him, but the Argentine sees a first-time shot blocked.
Endo becomes the first Liverpool player to see yellow for a foul on halfway.

GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLL! SALAH ADDS A THIRD! That is surely game over as Liverpool punish some abysmal Brentford defending! Kelleher sends a straightforward kick up into the Brentford half, where Gakpo outjumps Ajer to glance it on.
Both Collins and Mee hesitate and end up leaving the loose ball to Salah, who bustles into the area, holds off his marker and finishes across Flekken.
3-0 to the leaders – they are going five points clear!

Gakpo gets the assist for his fellow substitute, flicking Kelleher's long kick into his path, but what are Collins and Mee doing? They both left the ball for each other, and Salah took full advantage.
Salah now has six goal involvements in five league games against Brentford (five goals, one assist), scoring in each of his previous three league games against the Bees.
His latest effort has surely put this match beyond Frank's men.
PENALTY APPEAL! Reguilon gets up the left wing to cross for Toney, who is clattered from behind by Robertson and goes down inside the area.
The Brentford fans scream for a spot-kick, then Endo – who is on a yellow – flies into a 50-50 with Onyeka.
Oliver penalises Onyeka, and the VAR clears the initial Robertson challenge – that was a risky one!
Onyeka is booked for his challenge on Endo, further irritating the home fans.
Liverpool were a little fortunate there, as Robertson got nowhere near the ball as he barged Toney over.
The argument might be that Toney knew what he was doing – he had a glance over his shoulder and anticipated the contact.
Frank makes his fourth change as Damsgaard replaces Jensen.
GOOOAAAALL! TONEY GETS ONE BACK! That's more like it from Brentford! Wissa darts onto a ball down the right-hand channel and finds Reguilon with his cutback, despite being caught late by Konate.
The left wing-back sees his shot brilliantly saved by Kelleher, but Toney is on hand to side-foot the rebound home.
It's 3-1 – they couldn't, could they?
Toney has netted his first Premier League goal against Liverpool on what is his fourth appearance against them in the competition.
That has given the home crowd a lift.
Brentford are just doing everything a little quicker now.
Full credit to Frank's side – they could have sunk without trace when Salah made it 3-0, but they have shown plenty of fight since then.
Liverpool are preparing their final two changes now.
Mac Allister looks for Diaz with a cute backheel inside a crowded penalty area, but it's just cut out.
That's better from Brentford as Flekken picks out Damsgaard in space with a neat, driven pass.
He advances over halfway before attempting to release Wissa, but Konate slides in to snuff out the danger.
We've got 10 minutes to play, with Brentford trying to set up a grandstand finish.
PENALTY APPEAL! Diaz sprints into the box, hitting the byline before chopping back as Collins dives in.
Oliver initially doesn't give a spot-kick, but replays show contact from the defender on the slide.
There's a VAR check in the background... no penalty is the decision, there wasn't enough in it to bring Diaz down.
Here come those Liverpool changes.
Elliott is on for one of the goalscorers, the impressive Mac Allister.
Gomez, meanwhile, is on for Bradley.
Klopp wraps his young full-back in cotton wool after seeing Alexander-Arnold ruled out of next week's cup final.
Frank responds by using his final change.
Ghoddos is back from the Asian Cup, and he replaces Reguilon.
GOOOOOOAAAAAAAALLL! GAKPO MAKES THE POINTS SAFE FOR LIVERPOOL! The visitors have four, and yet again, it's poor defending from Collins.
He fails to deal with a long ball down the right channel, then there's another error as Ghoddos allows Diaz's pass to slip under his boot and reach Gakpo.
He makes no mistake when bearing down on Flekken, opening up his body to finish on his left foot – 4-1!
Diaz gets the assist, slipping a pass infield to find Gakpo running through on goal.
Ghoddos should have cut it out, but individual errors cost Brentford again!
This is a real statement result for Liverpool, who have made a potentially tricky away game look routine.
Arsenal go to Burnley and Manchester City face Chelsea later on Saturday – how will the Reds' title rivals respond?
Before kick-off, Liverpool had 15 more points (54) than they had after 24 games of last season (39).
In three of the previous four top-flight campaigns where the Reds had at least 54 points after 24 games, they have finished second (in 1990-91, 2018-19 & 2021-22).
The other was in 2019-20, when they had 70 points at this stage and won the Premier League.
SAVE! Liverpool win a free-kick in an excellent position, slightly to the right of the D.
Salah surprisingly leaves it for Elliott, who sees a low, curling effort pushed away by Flekken.
We are into seven minutes of stoppage time here – that is a number the home fans weren't too pleased to see.
Endo is perhaps fortunate to walk away without a second yellow after catching Onyeka wide on the Brentford right.
The Bees will whip this free-kick into a crowded penalty area.
WHAT A SAVE! Brentford, and Toney, should have a second.
Toney meets Damsgaard's delivery with a glancing header at the near post, but Kelleher reacts with a great one-handed save, pushing it away before the Liverpool backline completes the clearance.
Brentford win another free-kick, this one in a much more central area.
Toney takes on the shot, but it deflects wide off the wall and the Bees fail to make the resulting corner count.
The hosts are going through the motions now at 4-1 down.
Diaz tip-toes past Collins as Liverpool continue to chase a fifth goal, but Janelt gets back to intercept his left-footed cutback.
Liverpool come back and win a corner, which Robertson will take from the left.
WOODWORK! Robertson's delivery finds Van Dijk completely unmarked, but the defender crashes his header off the top of the crossbar as Brentford avoid further damage.
That will be that at the Gtech!
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-4 LIVERPOOL.

The full-time whistle sounds in west London, and Liverpool pass what could have been a stern test of their title ambitions with flying colours! Nunez's chipped finish had the Reds ahead before half-time, and injuries to Jones and Jota failed to knock Klopp's side off their stride as they raced into a 3-0 lead after the break.
Mac Allister took in Salah's pass before sliding his finish past Flekken, then the Egyptian got himself on the scoresheet by punishing some terrible defending from Collins and Mee.
Toney pulled one back for Brentford, but the Bees were unable to rouse themselves late on as Diaz teed up Gakpo for a fourth.
Liverpool go five points clear at the summit, and they can now put their feet up and watch on as Arsenal and Manchester City take to the field later on Saturday.
That's all from the Gtech Community Stadium, so thank you for your company and goodbye!
